keyVerseText: Then shalt thou kill the ram, and take of his blood, and put it upon the tip of the right ear of Aaron, and upon the tip of the right ear of his sons, and upon the thumb of their right hand, and upon the great toe of their right foot, and sprinkle the blood upon the altar round about.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun תְּנוּךְ (tᵉnûwk) derives perhaps from the same root as אֲנָךְ (ʼănâk), which means plumb-line or plummet, suggesting an idea of extension or protraction. This etymological connection implies that תְּנוּךְ literally refers to the extremity or tip of something, emphasizing a precise, pointed end rather than a general area. This adds a layer of concreteness beyond the English gloss 'tip,' highlighting a focused point or pinnacle, such as the lobe of the ear.
usageInScripture: The word תְּנוּךְ appears eight times in the Pentateuch, consistently referring to the tip or lobe of the ear, as seen in ritual contexts like Exodus 29:20 and several passages in Leviticus. Its translation varies slightly—'it upon the tip,' 'upon the tip,' and 'and upon the tip'—but always underscores the exact placement of blood or anointing on the ear's extremity. This uniformity reveals the term's specialized use in sacrificial and consecration rites, where precise physical points on the body are symbolically significant.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding תְּנוּךְ as the precise tip or extremity enriches our grasp of the detailed nature of Old Testament worship and consecration. The careful marking of the ear's tip with blood symbolizes attentive hearing and obedience to God's commands, reflecting the believer's call to listen and respond faithfully. This meticulous attention to detail in ritual foreshadows Christ's perfect obedience and the believer's sanctification through His sacrifice. Recognizing the word's original meaning invites us to consider how God values our whole being, down to the smallest part, in our covenant relationship with Him.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 29:20 instructs the priest to place the ram's blood 'upon the tip of the right ear of Aaron, and upon the tip of the right ear of his sons,' highlighting the significance of this precise location. The use of תְּנוּךְ here emphasizes the extremity of the ear as a symbol of consecrated hearing and submission. This detail enriches the verse's portrayal of the priestly dedication, reminding us that true service to God involves attentive listening and wholehearted commitment, marked visibly by the blood of atonement.
